newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's first oilfield starts oil parcel sales.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's first oilfield starts oil parcel sales.

text.p: South Africa's state-owned oil utilities, company Soekor and the Central Energy Fund, have started selling crude parcels from the country's first oilfield, after it passed the one million barrel output mark.
"A part load was delivered at Cape Town at the weekend," a Soekor spokesman told Reuters on Wednesday.
He was not able to say exactly how much had been landed in the parcel, which are amounts of oil smaller than tanker size.
The offshore Oribi oil field starting pumping oil on May 12 and delivered its first full tanker load of 700,000 barrels to the Chevron-Texaco joint venture, Caltex SA (Pty) Ltd on June 13.
By July 12, Oribi, which is 20 percent owned by Energy Africa, had produced one million barrels.

Soekor and CEF spokesmen said on Wednesday that the second tanker load had been bought by CEF as part of a joint marketing effort. CEF's Strategic Fuel Fund has storage tanks near the Caltex refinery at Milnerton where it can keep the oil until it is sold.
Asked who the oil might be sold to, the CEF spokesman said: "I am not sure that we can divulge that."
It was earlier reported that the buyer may be Total South Africa, which operates the inland Natref refinery with Sasol Ltd.
The Soekor spokesman said that the tanker was now back at the Oribi oil field 140 km (80 nautical miles) southwest of Mossel Bay on the east coast of South Africa.
He said that apart from disruption caused by bad weather, production at the oil field had been going well.
A spokesman for Caltex said that the first load had "met expectations" but that it was expensive.
CEF officials in May told the parliamentary minerals and energy committee that they expected the Oribi oil to be sold at a premium to benchmark North Sea Brent crude.
The Caltex spokesman said that the crude was lighter than Brent and was being mixed with straight run fuel to "heavy it up. It has performed as planned."
